name: Renovation & interior design contractors (category guide)
summary: HDB/condo reno permits, ID vs contractor scopes, deposit traps, and why tenant ‘light reno’ still needs landlord / MA sign-off.
body: Expat owners and long-stay tenants hit the same Reno pain: vague ID packages, milestone payment fights, and estate rules. Confirm whether you need HDB renovation permits, condo MA/MCST endorsement, or landlord consent before any hacking, wet-work, or balcony sealing. Separate design fees from main-con build quotes; demand a written schedule of works, variation-order rules, and retention sums. CASE threads warn about large upfront deposits with thin contracts — keep photos and WhatsApp change orders. Tenants: cosmetic painting and lighting still risk deposit deductions without written approval. Pair with furnishing and rental-inventory guides. Distinct from handyman call-outs for single trades. Category guide, not a ranked ID firm list.
whenToEngage: Need HDB / condo reno permit path before kicking off
ID package deposit large vs thin written scope
Tenant light reno — landlord / MA approval unclear
Variation-order / retention terms missing from quote
